expectations.text: The reply begins with a progress marker identifying Phase 1.
expectations.evidence: "**Phase 1 of 5 · Explore and choose a direction**" is the first line of the reply.

expectations.text: The reply includes a briefing with four labeled sections covering key debates, major voices, patterns, and open questions.
expectations.evidence: The briefing has bold headings "Key debates", "Major voices", "Patterns" and "Open questions".

expectations.text: The briefing is roughly 300 to 500 words long (it fails if under 250 or over 600 words).
expectations.evidence: The briefing, from "How widespread it is" through "Open questions", is about 400–450 words (URLs not counted). That is within 250–600.

expectations.text: The reply presents a mind map, either as an HTML page built from the skill's mind map template or as an indented text tree.
expectations.evidence: "I've saved an interactive map of possible angles as `.../mind-map.html`". The tool log shows the skill's templates/mind-map.html was read.

expectations.text: The mind map has 4 to 6 top-level angles, each with 2 or 3 narrower angles, and every angle has a saturation value between 0 and 1 (or, for a text tree, a crowdedness label).
expectations.evidence: The visible top-level angles are Student achievement (3 children), Teacher recruitment and retention (2), Budgets and cost savings (2) and Students' health and safety. Every angle shown has a saturation between 0 and 1, e.g. "saturation": 0.8, 0.55. The file is shortened, so later branches can't be checked, but everything visible conforms.

expectations.text: No mind map label is phrased as a research question; labels are short topics.
expectations.evidence: The labels are short topics, not questions: "Student achievement", "Instructional time kept or lost", "Stated preferences vs. measured turnover", "Where the cuts land".

expectations.text: The reply does not tell the user which angle they should choose or which one is best.
expectations.evidence: The reply only asks "explore the map and tell me which direction pulls you most" and recommends no angle.

expectations.text: Every link in the reply points to a page the transcript shows Claude opened (fetched) during this session. Every DOI (as a doi.org link or as text) either was opened itself or appears exactly in the list of DOIs found on pages Claude opened (shown under FILES or DOIS ON OPENED PAGES). A DOI seen only in search results doesn't count. Links and DOIs in the mind map count too.
expectations.evidence: Every link in the reply and the mind map (ncsl, edweek, educationnext, chalkbeat, PMC8595551, PMC9979633, nwea) appears in the WebFetch log. No DOIs are cited.

expectations.text: The reply asks the user which direction interests them and why.
expectations.evidence: "tell me which direction pulls you most, and why."

expectations.text: The reply asks the user no more than two questions.
expectations.evidence: There are two questions: "where does your thinking on four-day school weeks stand right now...?" and "which direction pulls you most, and why". "Ask me how I know..." is an invitation to the user, not a question put to them.
